knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The guide sequence is wash, cover, glove and report. A loose tissue, a rub alone or waiting does not meet the requirement.
A cut is a portal of entry, which is why it must be covered. The other options are wrong, since dressings do not replace hand hygiene.
A skin condition is reported to the supervisor, who decides what tasks are safe. Self-diagnosis and disinfectant on the skin are not the approved steps.

practicalCriteria: Given a simulated cut, the learner washes, covers, gloves and reports in the correct order before continuing.
Given a rash scenario, the learner stops the task, reports to the supervisor and does not diagnose.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation of the simulated cut sequence
Incident or injury record completed for the simulation
stopWorkCriteria: A cut or abrasion is open and not covered: stop before handling any body fluid, sharp, linen or waste.
A skin condition is present: stop and report before any further task.
